newsitem.title: USA: U.S. talking to Peru, Japan about hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. talking to Peru, Japan about hostage crisis.

text.p: The United States expressed concern on Wednesday over a hostage situation in Peru where leftist rebels were holed up in the Japanese ambassador's residence and threatening to kill at least 200 captives.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry declined to say whether any American diplomats were among those being held. He said the United States had engaged in "very extensive overnight conversations" with the governments of Peru and Japan.
Asked if the United States had been asked to provide hostage rescue personnel, McCurry said: "I'm going to decline comment on that."

"The United States is obviously concerned about the situation, and we remain in very close contact with those authorities in Peru addressing the situation," McCurry told reporters. "We're concerned because a group of international diplomats apparently are at the facility and there's an incident that jeopardises their well-being."

The armed stand-off was unresolved on Wednesday morning following Tuesday night's spectacular assault on the residence during which heavily armed rebels attacked the building from outside while, according to some versions, guerrillas disguised as waiters joined in from the inside.
Asked if Americans were among those held captive, McCurry said: "It serves no useful purpose for the United States government to talk about who may or may not be at the facility."
